title: Authority separation
body:
Intention Service dynamically discovers/re-evaluates viable intentions, asks clarification, and READY-gates dispatch. The architecture module consumes it; do not create fixed permanent action catalogs.

ConnectSelector owns the route-selection binding for DIRECT, RPC and QUEUE and their actual capability/explain evidence. JMS bridging remains distinct, with acknowledgement, transactions, redelivery, ordering, idempotency and DLQ explicit. Never claim Queue enqueue is synchronous completion. Network transport/socket selection, serialization codec and RPC envelope are separate authorities.

Identity/authentication must be attached to individual principals/trust boundaries, not set once globally. External authority owns authentication assertions and legal conclusions. CRM owns relationship truth; Relationship Case owns case coordination and typed references; NotNotes owns document truth; Institutional Policy owns published policy; Brand Interaction/Governance owns its own evidence and choices, never third-party reputation truth.

SSC owns component/lineage/source levels and reachable ::requires closure, qualified immutable dependency locks. Deployment owns target artifact selection, executable package loadability, REXX_PATH, activation and verification. Architecture Intentions only emits unresolved build requests and receives externally verified SSC evidence.

A human design sign-off is not a cryptographic approval. Promotion revalidates the selected comparison and requires a trusted external approval verifier; generation changes require new review. No route choice, review, or SSC receipt itself authorizes execution.
summary: Intention Service dynamically discovers/re-evaluates viable intentions, asks clarification, and READY-gates dispatch. The architecture module consumes it; do not create fixed permanent action catalogs.
invariants: Architecture selection and review never authorize execution
Unknown qualification fails closed and remains visible
Each external component retains its own semantic and provenance authority

provenance.claim: Exact historical baseline; no new runtime acceptance
